 Predictions Denmark and Norway meet in the UEFA Nations League on Tuesday, November 17, at Parken Stadium in Copenhagen, Denmark, with kickoff set for 2:45 p.m. ET. Denmark is favored to win, with a 2.32x payout on PrizePicks, while the underdog Norway has a 2.43x payout.
 Denmark will advance to the Nations League quarterfinals with any result other than a defeat on Tuesday, but a win gives them a chance to clinch the top spot in Group A4. Norway must find a way to claim victory to avoid a disappointing third-place finish in the group and a spot in the relegation playoff. 
 Below, we’ll break down our Denmark vs. Norway prediction and picks for Tuesday afternoon’s UEFA Nations League match, including the spread, total goals, and key player picks for PrizePicks.

 The reverse fixture between these Scandanavian sides saw Norway claim a narrow 3-2 defeat in September. Norway sailed to victory following 2 goals inside 18 minutes, but they needed a 74th-minute winner from ST Erling Haaland to offset a pair of Danish goals to claim all three points. 
 However, Denmark’s convincing 4-1 win over Portugal over the weekend sees them holding the advantage coming into the final matchday. ST Rasmus Højlund scored twice in seven minutes to blow open a 1-0 match, and Portugal’s stoppage time consolation goal did nothing to take away from Denmark’s dominant performance away from home.
 Højlund’s 5 goals in the competition trail only Harry Kane’s 8 strikes, as he paces a Danish attack that leads Group A4 with 11 goals. That said, they may need just one tally on Tuesday to claim top spot in the group. 
 According to PrizePicks, they have a 5.88x payout to finish atop Group A4 should they get a win combined with a Portugal defeat to Wales.
 Denmark’s biggest injury concern is the fitness of CB Joachim Andersen, who came off in the final minutes of the Portugal match with a knock. However, manager Brian Riemer has said it’s nothing serious, and he looks to be available. LB Patrick Dorgu is out of the squad with a thigh issue, as he dropped out before the Portugal match.
 Wales host Portugal in Cardiff and Denmark host Norway in Copenhagen on Tuesday at 19:45 GMT in UEFA Nations League Group A4 Matchday 6.

 Norway’s performance post-World Cup has been disappointing, to say the least. Their 2-1 defeat to Portugal can be excused, but it was the 2-1 shock loss away to Wales — who played the entire second half down a man — that puts them in a must-win situation.
 They got revenge over the weekend with a 3-1 victory in Oslo, but Wales made it interesting with a 79th-minute goal before Erling Haaland’s late penalty sealed all three points. The goal was just his fourth of the competition, a low number by his standards. Norway will need him to step up in this match if they are to qualify from the group.
 Stale Solbakken is without ST Jorgen Strand Larsen, who misses out with an ankle injury, but he should get CAM Martin Ødegaard back in the lineup after he was a stoppage-time substitute against Wales due to illness. 
 Denmark have won three of the last five matchups with Norway, with the reverse fixture being their only defeat in the last seven meetings. The Danes will also hope to find the back of the net first, as all five of their matches in the Nations League have been won by the side who opened the scoring.

 Denmark vs. Norway Prediction on Winner – 11/17/26
 Here are the key game stats and trends behind our Denmark vs. Norway prediction on the winner for Tuesday’s UEFA Nations League match.
 Norway’s two away fixtures in this year’s Nations League saw them fall by identical 2-1 scorelines at Wales and Portugal, respectively.
 Dating back to the spring, Norway have gone four matches without claiming victory outside their national borders. They’ve lost three of those matches by the same 2-1 scoreline, with only a 1-1 draw in a New York City warm-up friendly seeing them get a result. 
 Norway’s backline is the fifth-leakiest of the 16 teams in Group A, conceding 1.8 goals per 90 minutes. At the other end, they’ve managed just 9 goals in five matches after scoring 13 goals in six at the World Cup.
 Denmark has been lethal at the offensive end, with their 6 missed big chances tied with Wales for the fewest in the competition. They’re also utilizing set pieces to their advantage, leading all nations with 4 set-piece goals, per FotMob . 
 This is an area where they could exploit Norway’s defense. According to WhoScored , 4 of the 9 goals Norway have conceded in the competition have come from set pieces.

 According to WhoScored , Højlund has attempted exactly 5 shots in each of his last two Nations League outings and 17 over five matches.
 He’s attempted multiple shots in all five outings, with 3+ shots in three. That includes the reverse fixture, where he scored a goal on 3 efforts at goal.
 Norway will be forced to throw bodies forward if they’re level or trailing, which could open things up on the counter-attack for the pacey Højlund.
 As we discussed earlier, Norway are prone to being hurt on set pieces. The 6-foot-3 Højlund presents an aerial threat, and he’s averaging 0.43 headed shots per 90 minutes during the tournament .

 Denmark are allowing opponents to put 48.2% of their shots in the competition on target. That’s the most of any Group A nation, per FBRef , and second most of any nation in all the Nations League — behind only Luxembourg.
 Haaland ranks fourth among all Nations League Group A players with 2.3 shots on target per 90 minutes .
 In the reverse fixture, Haaland bagged a brace with both goals coming from open play. 
 Haaland has scored in both his career fixtures against Denmark, including a June 2024 friendly where Denmark won 3-1 at home.
